newsitem.title: SURINAM: Strike ends at Alcoa Suriname unit.
newsitem.headline: Strike ends at Alcoa Suriname unit.

text.p: A strike over pay hitting U.S. aluminium giant Alcoa's unit in Suriname, Suralco, ended on Friday when all sides agreed to resume talks to solve the labor dispute, Suralco officials said.

Most of the 2,000 workers at Suralco Paranam alumina plant, 20 miles (30 km) south of the capital Paramaribo, had stopped work on Tuesday, a crippling stoppage for the small country's main export earner. The strike cost Suralco about $2 million, Suralco spokesman Cor Lie A Kwie told Reuters.
He said talks would resume with the government-appointed mediation council. He gave no details.

Another strike which started Monday at a bauxite plant in Parana district run by Billiton, an affiliate of South Africa's Gencor was going on, officials said. The plant employs about 500 workers, who reject a new collective bargaining agreement. It sells all its production to Suralco.

Suralco union leaders have asked for a 175 percent wage increase over one year. Management has so far offered 60 percent. Government mediators have proposed a 75 percent raise in the first year and 60 percent in the following nine months.
Suralco management said Friday that accepting the mediators' plan would cost up to 600 jobs.
Suralco, 60 percent owned by Alcoa and 40 percent by Australia's Western Mining WMC.AXu, produces an average 4,500 tonnes of alumina per day.
About 95 percent of its production is exported, mostly to the United States. The company's exports account for about 75 percent, or $300 million, of Suriname's total export earnings.
